title: Verify and prune the cached apt archives
description: Follow-up from TASK-1.39 security review and judge (J-1-01, J-1-03): apt trusts a .deb already in /var/cache/apt/archives on name and size, not hash, so a .deb planted in the Actions cache by code in a main job would be installed as root on later runs for up to a month. restore-keys also carries old .debs forward month to month.

nodes.title: Verify and prune the cached apt archives
Bootstrap the strict TypeScript project with one-command checks
Run every check in GitHub Actions on each push and pull request
Retry the stalled Playwright system-dependency install in CI
Keep strict wall-clock speed checks out of the CI test run
Recover dpkg and harden the remaining test timeouts

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a restored .deb whose sha256 does not match the signed index (apt-cache show <pkg>=<ver> after apt-get update), When the restore step runs, Then that file is discarded before reaching /var/cache/apt/archives, and a test proves a tampered file is dropped

Given the job runs later steps (tests, E2E) after the installs, When the apt cache is saved, Then it is saved right after Collect (actions/cache/restore + actions/cache/save) so later steps cannot add files to it

Given last month's cache is restored via restore-keys, When Collect runs, Then .debs no longer needed by the current install are not carried forward (e.g. apt-get autoclean or collect only what this install used)
